unspecified_scores.reason: Each time the iOS shell loads or reloads a page, AppShell's content remounts once after hydration. A video page opened at that moment loses its first player instance and its fetches, and the user sees a flash or a restart.

On a desktop with a long settings panel open, a wheel over the panel scrolls the page behind it instead of the panel. A trackpad pinch over the player also scrolls the page instead of zooming, and horizontal swipes do nothing.

Pseudo full screen is the fallback when element full screen is refused, which on a wheel-equipped desktop is rare. There a wheel scrolls the hidden canvas, so the page is at a different scroll position when the user exits.
Each render of the file page's slot publishes to the store and re-renders the layer's player tree with the latest props. That is the intended way props reach the player and the user sees nothing.

specification_compliance: The touch-point list omits pseudo-fullscreen.spec.ts, spec-viewport.spec.ts, three workbench desktop specs, row-action-reveal.test.ts and FilePreview.slot.test.tsx (TP-1 to TP-5 confirmed).
I1 says that in the iOS shell the player is inside the slot. The final state holds that, but after hydration the provider is first enabled and then switched off, which remounts the subtree (B-1).
I7 (a wheel scrolls the same as without the layer) holds for vertical page scrolls. It does not hold for a scrollable panel inside the player, for horizontal deltas or for ctrl+wheel (B-2).

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: In system (element) full screen, the full-screen element is inside the layer's frame, so a wheel over it reaches the frame's onWheel. The handler does not check isFullscreenNow and scrolls the canvas hidden behind the full-screen player.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: A desktop user who scrolls the wheel while watching full screen comes back to the page at a different scroll position on exit.

regression_risks: The iOS shell's post-hydration remount of AppShell's children can restart a video page's first load.
The layer's wheel handler blocks scrolling inside the player's settings panel and blocks trackpad pinch-zoom over the player.
